correctness.rationale: For two-cell averaging, exactly 2r cyclic edges cross color classes, giving V(Px)=2r|ell(x)|. The mean difference ell has zero-sum coefficients and discrete antiderivative S, so the exact cyclic BV dual norm is (max S−min S)/2, with attainment by two opposite edge jumps / interval indicators. Each positive and negative color-run increment is at most this range; equality K=1 forces each run mass to equal one r-th of its class. Conversely balanced increments alternate ±1/r and attain K=1. For r>=2, positive masses force every proper interval class-mass discrepancy to be <1, while concentration in adjacent opposite-color runs approaches 1; continuity realizes all [1,r). The accompanying exact Fraction checker independently compared the formula with every proper interval for 2010 cases and checked boundary cases. Finite enumeration supplements, does not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: Cyclic total variation controls neighboring-sample changes. A two-cell weighted conditional expectation is a canonical coarse-graining operator, yet its two cells may be noncontiguous and create many artificial boundaries. An exact linear-time norm invariant answers how much such a projection can amplify variation, characterizes all stable positive mass choices with an iff run-level balance law, and solves the full attainable amplification spectrum [1,r) for fixed interlaced color geometry. This is a motivated complete classification, not a numerical slice or a generic BV duality observation.
